title: Compare without PCs and without QC

blocks.what_we_do: Compare the main analysis, which we planned in advance, with two analyses that we deliberately make weaker.
blocks.why:
In the first comparison, we leave out the [PCs](../docs/glossary.md#pca-pc). PCs are the numbers that summarise ancestry. We keep the same cleaned cohort and the same [covariates](../docs/glossary.md#covariate), age and sex. This shows the effect of the PC adjustment alone.

In the second comparison, we start from the state saved at module 2. It has the case and control labels and the corrected strands. We use no sample [QC](../docs/glossary.md#qc), no variant QC and no PCs. This comparison changes the samples and the variants as well as the QC. We cannot give its differences to one single cause. The label "no QC" does not mean that we undid the strand correction or the case and control labels. When you interpret the differences, compare the shared variants and the number of samples for each variant.
blocks.you_need: The state from step 5.7, the state from step 2.8, the summary statistics file from step 6.8 for the main analysis, the covariates and the original sample information. The two comparison scans are new PLINK reports. R puts them into the same standard columns in memory. In this way, all three analyses are summarised in the same way.
blocks.command:
```{r s7-7}
no_pc <- guided_path(cfg, "7.7", "no_pcs")
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "5.7"), "--maf", "0.01", "--covar", guided_path(cfg, "6.3", "covariates.tsv"),
  "--covar-name", "Age", "--covar-variance-standardize", "--glm", "sex", "hide-covar", "firth-fallback", "--out", no_pc))
metadata <- guided_metadata(cfg)
all_covar <- metadata[c("FID", "IID", "Age")]; names(all_covar)[1] <- "#FID"
all_file <- guided_path(cfg, "7.7", "all_ages.tsv"); guided_write(all_covar, all_file)
no_qc <- guided_path(cfg, "7.7", "no_qc_no_pcs")
baseline <- guided_path(cfg, "2.8")
if (!file.exists(paste0(baseline, ".pgen"))) baseline <- file.path(cfg$data_dir, "checkpoints", "2.8", "state")
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", baseline, "--maf", "0.01", "--covar", all_file,
  "--covar-name", "Age", "--covar-variance-standardize", "--glm", "sex", "hide-covar", "firth-fallback", "--out", no_qc))
main <- guided_summary_stats(cfg)
a <- guided_standardise_scan(guided_association(no_pc))
b <- guided_standardise_scan(guided_association(no_qc))
k <- match(main$variant_id, a$variant_id)
stopifnot(!anyNA(k), all(main$n == a$n[k]))
autosomal_p <- function(x) x$p_value[x$chromosome %in% as.character(1:22)]
summarise <- function(x) c(finite_tests = sum(valid_p(x$p_value)), hits = sum(x$p_value[valid_p(x$p_value)] < 5e-8),
  lambda = lambda_gc(autosomal_p(x)))
comparison <- rbind(main = summarise(main), no_PCs = summarise(a), no_sample_or_variant_QC_no_PCs = summarise(b))
print(comparison)
stopifnot(comparison[2, "hits"] == 15L, comparison[3, "hits"] == 19L)
guided_write(data.frame(model = rownames(comparison), comparison, row.names = NULL), guided_path(cfg, "7.7", "comparison.tsv"))
save_plot(guided_path(cfg, "7.7", "qq_comparison.png"), function() {
  par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
  plotted <- list(autosomal_p(main), autosomal_p(a), autosomal_p(b))
  limits <- c(0, max(-log10(unlist(plotted))))
  plot_qq(autosomal_p(main), "QC + ten PCs", ylim = limits)
  plot_qq(autosomal_p(a), "QC, no PCs", ylim = limits)
  plot_qq(autosomal_p(b), "No sample/variant QC, no PCs", ylim = limits)
}, width = 2100, height = 750)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s5-7_state --maf 0.01 --covar results/guided/s6-3_covariates.tsv --covar-name Age --covar-variance-standardize --glm sex hide-covar firth-fallback --out results/guided/s7-7_no_pcs --threads 2 --memory 2048
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s2-8_state --maf 0.01 --covar results/guided/s7-7_all_ages.tsv --covar-name Age --covar-variance-standardize --glm sex hide-covar firth-fallback --out results/guided/s7-7_no_qc_no_pcs --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--glm sex hide-covar firth-fallback` fits the association model with the recorded sex, reports only the genetic tests and uses Firth correction when needed. `--covar` loads the covariate table, which is matched by sample ID. `--covar-variance-standardize` rescales numerical covariates so the fitting is stable. `--covar-name Age` keeps only age and so leaves out the PCs on purpose. The first call keeps the cleaned cohort. The second call changes `--pfile` to the state before QC and uses the ages of all wells. `--maf 0.01` stays as a rule for which variants are tested, also in the comparison without QC. `--out` keeps the outputs apart; threads and memory are unchanged.
blocks.expected_result:
Main analysis: 236,815 tests, eight hits, lambda about 1.016. Without PCs after QC: 236,815 tests, 15 hits, lambda about 1.546. Without sample or variant QC and without PCs: 239,647 tests, 19 hits, lambda about 1.655. The extra peaks do not show that worse QC finds more true causes.

The tested PLINK version is set in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: the executable chunks, the comparisons with the expected results and the final plot checks passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the input file that R names and the previous step. Keep the command and the messages from the console. Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
Can we interpret the comparison of the main analysis with the no-PC analysis more narrowly than the comparison with the no-QC analysis?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

Yes. The first comparison keeps the same samples and the same number of samples for each variant. The second comparison also changes the samples and the tested sites.

</details>
blocks.files_created: Two comparison association outputs, the age table, `s7-7_comparison.tsv` and `s7-7_qq_comparison.png`.

if (requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE)) knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = getwd())

cfg <- guided_init()
setwd(start_dir)

figures.gemini_prompt: Create a labelled teaching schematic for Compare without PCs and without QC. Use shapes and text as well as colour. Do not invent numeric course results, gene annotations or individual identities. This complements the tested R plot; it does not replace it.
figures.alt_text: QQ plots share a vertical scale; removing PCs and then sample and variant QC increases median inflation.
